The project is a real Godot 4 project with the required layout and clean headless launch, the title screen, and a chapter menu showing four chapters of six level buttons. Runtime inspection shows rewind and ghosts exist, but gameplay is severely unpolished: the player can leave the world platform and fall unbounded (y>34000) with no recovery, the near_victory run never reached the exit so completion metrics were never shown, the title trace replays non-deterministically, and ghost switch/door/laser/enemy interaction and reset were never exercised. Crucially, the level content in LevelData.gd is a degenerate near-uniform template - chapters 1/2/3/4 all reduce to collecting switches/plates, no level requires two ghosts to reach the exit, and no temporal-coordination puzzle exists - contradicting the instruction's core vision and 'not a prototype / polished vertical slice' requirement. All art is host-declared mock placeholder (art_manifest), so final art is unmet. This is not ready: many criteria are untested, several instruction requirements are unmet or contradicted, and remaining major/blocker issues are open.", "instruction_audit": "The instruction is specific enough to design against: 30-second loop, ghost replay, four-layer loops, timeline bar, exit gating, reset, completion metrics, 24 levels across four chapters, asset libraries, fixed project layout, exact headless command, scenario mechanism, 1-10 traces under demo_outputs, 600-frame cap, and deterministic replay. Two points are inherently unobservable by a text-only reviewer without pixels: the title-screen visual (clock hands and ghost silhouettes) and any screenshot-based polish claim; these must be verified by rendered inspection, not asserted. The instruction's asset section provides library mounts but the art_manifest reports both mounted libraries unavailable in this environment and substitutes mock placeholders; this is acceptable as an experiment fixture but the instruction's requirement to select/copy library packs is not satisfiable from the mock path and must be tracked as an open design/asset gap for the next iteration. No mandatory scenario list is specified, so the Designer's authored scenario names (near_rewind, near_victory, etc.) are a valid design choice and not a conflict.
